1969Conference paper

Mathematical reasoning

CARPS reasons over calculus word problems

Structured descriptions of objects helped a program interpret a limited class of calculus rate problems.

Eugene Charniak

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

ReasoningMathematical reasoningNatural language processingKnowledge representation

The contribution

CARPS gathered information about objects across sentences and connected different expressions referring to the same object. These structures helped transform word problems into a form suitable for mathematical solution. The paper reported fourteen examples, mostly drawn from textbooks, illustrating how domain knowledge could support language interpretation.

What this does not establish

The system covered a limited class of rate problems, and some source problems were modified. These examples are not a general calculus benchmark or evidence of unrestricted language understanding.

Why this date?

1969 dates this IJCAI conference paper, rather than the earlier thesis version of CARPS.
